At sixteen thirty, and it's sixteen ten now.

We have an inspection on the eighteenth. Can you be back before then?
Yes, sir. I can come back on the seventeenth.
All right. Change the dates on your form, and I'll sign it.

L74.text: Excuse me, do you have the time?

L77.text: The tires we ordered were delivered on Monday, the day before yesterday.

L78.text: Everyone's waiting for you at the restaurant. How soon can you get here?

Then one of them will make two trips. It'll take longer, but we'll get it done.

L80.text: It's almost five o'clock. Can you still send me the delivery schedule today?
Sorry, I can't. I'll send it first thing in the morning.

L82.text: Do I need an appointment for sick call, or can I just walk in?

L85.text: We've run out of toner for the printer, and the new order won't arrive until Thursday.

All the trucks are out, but you can take the pickup.

Not for long. It's supposed to rain later this afternoon.

L87.text: How was the food at the new dining facility?

L95.text: What's the weather supposed to be like this weekend?

Oh, no. So we're back to square one. I'll fill out the forms again this afternoon.

L99.text: You've already signed for your room key, haven't you?

By the end of next week.

Travel, and spend time with my grandchildren.

L1018.text: The Grand Canyon is about two hundred and seventy-seven miles long and up to eighteen miles wide. It was formed over millions of years by the Colorado River cutting through rock. Today, more than five million people visit it every year.

L1019.text: Sleep is very important for good health. Adults need seven to nine hours of sleep each night. People who do not sleep enough are more likely to have accidents and to get sick.

L1020.text: The Wright brothers made the first powered airplane flight in 1903, at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina. The first flight lasted only twelve seconds and covered about one hundred twenty feet.

L1021.text: Honeybees are important to farmers because they carry pollen from flower to flower. This helps plants produce fruit and seeds. Without bees, many of the foods we eat would become rare and expensive.

L1022.text: The Statue of Liberty was a gift from France to the United States. It was completed in 1886 and stands on an island in New York Harbor. It has become a symbol of freedom around the world.

L1023.text: Drinking enough water is especially important in hot weather. When you sweat, your body loses water and salt. If you do not replace them, you can become dizzy and weak. Soldiers in the field should drink water regularly, even if they are not thirsty.

L1024.text: The Pacific Ocean is the largest and deepest ocean on Earth. It covers about one third of the planet's surface. Its deepest point, the Mariana Trench, is nearly seven miles deep.

L1025.text: The Internet began as a military research project in the late 1960s. At first, it connected only a few universities and government offices. It became popular with the public in the 1990s, when the World Wide Web made it easy to use.

L1026.text: Regular exercise has many benefits. It strengthens the heart, helps control weight, and improves mood. Experts recommend at least thirty minutes of moderate exercise, such as fast walking, five days a week.

L1027.text: Alaska is the largest state in the United States, more than twice the size of Texas. However, it has one of the smallest populations. Much of the state is covered by mountains, forests, and ice.

L1028.text: Abraham Lincoln was the sixteenth president of the United States. He led the country during the Civil War and helped end slavery. He was killed in 1865, just days after the war ended.

L1029.text: The human heart beats about one hundred thousand times a day. It pumps blood through the body, carrying oxygen to every organ. Regular exercise and a healthy diet help keep the heart strong.

L1030.text: Mount Everest, on the border of Nepal and China, is the highest mountain in the world. It is about twenty-nine thousand feet tall. The first people to reach the top were Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay, in 1953.

L1031.text: Many accidents at home happen in the kitchen. To stay safe, turn pot handles toward the back of the stove, keep knives out of children's reach, and never leave cooking food unattended.

L1032.text: The Mississippi River is one of the longest rivers in North America. It flows about two thousand three hundred miles, from Minnesota to the Gulf of Mexico. For centuries, it has been an important route for trade.

L1033.text: The Moon has no air and no water. Its surface is covered with dust and craters. Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon between 1969 and 1972, during the Apollo missions.

L1034.text: Washing your hands is one of the best ways to prevent illness. Use soap and warm water, and wash for at least twenty seconds. This removes germs that can cause colds and the flu.

L1035.text: George Washington was the first president of the United States. Before that, he was the commander of the army during the War of Independence. The capital city, Washington, D.C., is named after him.

L1036.text: Deserts receive less than ten inches of rain a year. Although they are often very hot during the day, they can be very cold at night because there are few clouds to hold the heat.

L1037.text: Smoking damages almost every organ in the body. It is a major cause of heart disease and lung cancer. People who stop smoking, even after many years, quickly improve their health.

L1038.text: The Great Lakes are five large lakes on the border between the United States and Canada. Together, they hold about one fifth of all the fresh water on the Earth's surface.

L1039.text: Thomas Edison is famous for developing the first practical electric light bulb in 1879. He also worked on the phonograph and motion pictures. During his life, he received more than one thousand patents.

L1040.text: A healthy breakfast gives you energy for the morning. Good choices include whole grains, fruit, and eggs or yogurt. People who skip breakfast are often hungrier later and eat more unhealthy snacks.

L1041.text: Hurricanes are large storms that form over warm ocean water. They bring strong winds, heavy rain, and flooding. In the United States, hurricane season lasts from June to November.

L1042.text: The Panama Canal connects the Atlantic and Pacific Oceans. Before it opened in 1914, ships had to sail around South America, a trip of thousands of extra miles.

L1043.text: Vitamin D helps the body build strong bones. The body makes vitamin D when the skin is in sunlight. It is also found in fish, eggs, and milk.

L1044.text: The American flag has thirteen stripes and fifty stars. The stripes stand for the original thirteen colonies, and the stars stand for the fifty states.

L1045.text: Earthquakes happen when large pieces of the Earth's crust move suddenly. California has many earthquakes because it sits on the edge of two of these pieces. Most earthquakes are small, but some cause great damage.

L1046.text: The first transcontinental railroad in the United States was completed in 1869. It connected the east and west coasts and reduced the trip across the country from months to about a week.

L1047.text: Stress can affect your body as well as your mind. It can cause headaches, trouble sleeping, and high blood pressure. Exercise, enough sleep, and talking with friends can help reduce stress.

L1048.text: Penguins are birds, but they cannot fly. Instead, they are excellent swimmers. They use their wings like flippers to move quickly through the water. Most penguins live in the Southern Hemisphere.

L1049.text: The Pentagon, near Washington, D.C., is the headquarters of the U.S. Department of Defense. It is one of the largest office buildings in the world. It was completed in 1943, during World War Two.

L1050.text: Bicycles are a cheap and healthy way to travel. Riders should always wear a helmet and use lights at night. In many cities, special bike lanes make riding safer.

L1051.text: The Sun is a star. It is about ninety-three million miles from the Earth. Its light takes about eight minutes to reach us. Without the Sun's energy, there would be no life on Earth.

L1052.text: Many people believe that eating carrots improves your eyesight. Carrots contain vitamin A, which is important for healthy eyes. However, eating extra carrots will not make normal eyes see better.

L1053.text: The Civil War in the United States lasted from 1861 to 1865. It was fought between the northern and southern states. More Americans died in this war than in any other war in the nation's history.

L1054.text: Recycling saves energy and natural resources. For example, making a new can from recycled aluminum uses much less energy than making one from raw materials. Paper, glass, and plastic can also be recycled.

L1055.text: Lightning is very dangerous. During a thunderstorm, you should stay indoors and away from windows. If you are outside, avoid tall trees and open fields.

L1056.text: The Golden Gate Bridge in San Francisco opened in 1937. At the time, it was the longest suspension bridge in the world. Its famous orange color helps ships see it in the fog.

L1057.text: Too much sugar is bad for your teeth and your health. Many drinks, like soda and juice, contain a lot of sugar. Water and milk are healthier choices.

L1058.text: The Amazon rainforest in South America is the largest tropical rainforest in the world. It is home to millions of kinds of plants and animals. It also produces a large part of the world's oxygen.

L1059.text: The first modern Olympic Games were held in Athens, Greece, in 1896. Today, the Summer and Winter Games are each held every four years, two years apart. Athletes from over two hundred countries take part.

L1060.text: Sunburn is caused by the sun's ultraviolet rays. It can happen even on cloudy days. To protect your skin, use sunscreen, wear a hat, and avoid the strongest sun between ten and four.

L1061.text: Benjamin Franklin was a writer, scientist, and diplomat. He is famous for his experiments with electricity, including flying a kite in a thunderstorm. He also helped write the Declaration of Independence.

L1062.text: Volcanoes form where hot melted rock, called magma, rises to the surface. When a volcano erupts, the magma comes out as lava. Hawaii's islands were formed by volcanoes.

L1063.text: Good posture is important when you work at a desk. Keep your feet flat on the floor, your back straight, and the computer screen at eye level. Take a short break every hour to stretch.

L1064.text: The Liberty Bell is a famous symbol of American independence. It is kept in Philadelphia. The bell has a large crack and has not been rung for more than a hundred years.

L1065.text: Snakes are cold-blooded animals. This means their body temperature changes with the temperature around them. That is why snakes often lie in the sun in the morning to warm up.

L1066.text: Too much noise can damage your hearing. Soldiers on the firing range must always wear ear protection. Hearing loss from loud noise is permanent and cannot be cured.

L1067.text: The Erie Canal opened in 1825 and connected the Great Lakes to the Hudson River and New York City. It made shipping goods much cheaper and helped New York become the country's largest city.

L1068.text: The common cold is caused by a virus. Antibiotics do not work against viruses, so they cannot cure a cold. Rest, fluids, and time are the best treatment.

L1069.text: Dolphins are mammals, not fish. They breathe air through a hole on the top of their heads. They are very intelligent and communicate with each other using clicks and whistles.

L2440.text: Did you catch anything at the lake this morning?
Not a thing. But it was so peaceful out there that I didn't really care.

L2441.text: How do you get to work now that your car's been sold?
A neighbor drives me in, and I pay her for half the gas.

L2442.text: Does the soup of the day have any nuts in it? My son is allergic.
I'm not sure. Let me ask the chef before you order it.

L2443.text: What are you getting your parents for their fortieth anniversary?
My sister and I are chipping in to send them on a cruise.

L2444.text: You look exhausted. Didn't you sleep well?
Not really. The neighbor's car alarm kept going off until about three a.m.

L2445.text: Does this dress come in a smaller size?
Not in blue, I'm afraid. We've got your size in black, though, if you'd like to try it on.

L2446.text: Is everyone in your group doing their share of the project?
Everyone except Tom. He hasn't shown up to a single meeting, so the rest of us have been covering for him.

L2447.text: I can't log in to my bank account online. It keeps saying my password is wrong.
Click on 'Forgot password,' and they'll send a code to your phone so you can reset it.

L2448.text: Did you and Kevin decide on the house on Maple Avenue?
We loved it, but it was way over our budget, so we're still looking.

L2449.text: Hello? Jim? You keep cutting out. I only heard every other word.
Sorry, I'm in an elevator. Let me call you back in two minutes.

L2450.text: Is there a gas station near here? The light on my dashboard just came on.
There's one about two miles ahead, right after the bridge. You should make it.

L2451.text: Is Danny still taking swimming lessons at the community pool?
He was, but he's switched to soccer. He says it's more fun to play with his friends.

L2452.text: Do you know when the trash gets picked up on this street?
Tuesday mornings. But next week it's Wednesday because of the holiday on Monday.

L2453.text: How long is the wait for a table for four?
About forty-five minutes, but if you don't mind sitting at the counter, I can seat you right now.

L2454.text: Who won the basketball game between the officers and the sergeants?
The sergeants, but only by a single point, and that was in overtime.

L2455.text: There was a note on the door saying the mail carrier tried to deliver a package.
That means you'll have to pick it up at the post office, and bring your ID with you.

L2456.text: I heard your sister just had a baby. Boy or girl?
Twins, actually! One of each, so now I have a niece and a nephew.

L2457.text: Did you build that bookshelf yourself? It looks like it came from a store.
Thanks! I took a woodworking class last spring, and this is my first real project.

L2458.text: Would you like to buy an extended warranty for the TV? It's only thirty dollars.
No, thanks. It already comes with two years of coverage from the manufacturer.

L2459.text: Why are you taking the long way home?
Main Street's been closed since Monday for repairs, and it won't reopen until the end of the month.

L2460.text: Can I pick up my suits today? The ticket says they'll be ready Thursday.
Let me check. Yes, you're in luck. They finished them early this morning.

L2461.text: Have you registered for next semester's classes yet?
Not yet. I can't sign up until I pay a parking fine I got last fall.

L2462.text: Do you take credit cards, or should I go find an ATM?
Cards are fine, but there's a ten-dollar minimum. Your total is only seven fifty.

L2463.text: Our heating bill was almost double last month's.
No wonder. Somebody left the upstairs window open all weekend while we were away.

L2464.text: I tried to leave you a message yesterday, but your voicemail was full.
Oh, sorry about that. I never check it. Just send me a text next time.

L2465.text: Do you think I should pay off the furniture now or make monthly payments?

L2466.text: Did you ever hear back from the landlord about the broken window?

L2467.text: How often do your kids get to see their grandparents?

L2468.text: Excuse me, do you have these boots in a wider size?

L2469.text: Do you think watching American TV shows really helps your listening?

L2470.text: Are there any of those chocolate cookies left, or did the kids finish them?

L2471.text: Have you met the family that just moved in next door?

L2472.text: That new steak place was way too expensive for what we got, wasn't it?

L2473.text: Are you going to watch the soccer final at home or at the club?

L2474.text: Do you mind if I take this call? It's my daughter's school.

L2475.text: How do you manage to save money with three kids at home?

L2476.text: I'm thinking about buying the extended warranty on this laptop. Is it worth the money?

L2477.text: The final exam covers everything since the first week of class, doesn't it?

L2478.text: I'm afraid you've dialed the wrong number. Nobody named Kevin lives here.

L2479.text: Do you know whether family members can use the base pool on weekends?

L2480.text: Didn't you say you were allergic to peanuts? There are some in this salad.

L2481.text: How far in advance do we need to book the inspection before moving out of quarters?

L2482.text: Who's going to feed your cat while you're away on leave next month?

L2483.text: I need to send money to my parents back home. What's the cheapest way to do it?

L2484.text: Aren't you going to try out for the basketball team this season?

L2485.text: You couldn't lend me a pen for the test, could you? Mine just ran out of ink.

L2486.text: Attention, all visitors. The museum will close in thirty minutes. The gift shop will remain open for an extra fifteen minutes after closing. Thank you for visiting.

L2487.text: Hi, this is Tony from the gym. Your membership expires at the end of the month. If you renew this week, you'll get one month free. Stop by the front desk anytime.

L2488.text: Recruits, the uniform for tomorrow is the physical training uniform. We will run at oh six hundred and then go straight to breakfast. Do not be late.

L2489.text: Hello, this is the library. The book you reserved, "The History of Flight," is now available. We will hold it for you for five days at the front desk.

L2490.text: Good morning, passengers. Due to track work, this train will run express from Grand Street to Park Avenue. Passengers for stations in between should take the shuttle bus at Grand Street.

L2491.text: Attention, drivers. The gas station on base will be closed on Sunday for tank cleaning. Please fill up on Saturday or use the station outside the main gate.

L2492.text: The chaplain's office is open every weekday morning, and by appointment in the afternoon.

L2493.text: Only three of the eight trucks passed the safety inspection this morning.

L2494.text: The new dining hall can seat twice as many soldiers as the old one, which held two hundred.

L2495.text: The colonel said that leave requests for December must be turned in by November fifteenth.

L2496.text: How often is the shuttle on weekends?

L2497.text: Who's in charge of the kitchen today?

L2498.text: What time do the gates close at night?

L2499.text: Has your paycheck been deposited yet? Mine usually shows up on Friday.
Mine too, but with Friday's holiday, it won't go through until Monday.

L2500.text: That used car looks like a great deal. Are you going to buy it?
Not until my mechanic takes a look at it. A low price can hide a lot of problems.

L2501.text: I'm having trouble with these math problems. Could you go over them with me?
I'd be glad to, but math was never my strong point. You might be better off asking Lisa.

L2502.text: Did the trainees like the food?

L2503.text: This coupon says two for one on cereal. Can I use it here?
You could have yesterday. It expired at midnight, I'm afraid.

L2504.text: Are you still going camping this weekend?
We were, but the forecast calls for storms, so we've put it off until next month.

L2505.text: Is the training room free this afternoon?
The captain booked it until three.
I need it for an hour.
You can have it from three to four.

L2506.text: I want to take the sergeant's course next year.
You'll need a recommendation from your platoon leader.
A passing score on your last fitness test.
